To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the front speed is enhanced by a shear flow with an amplitude squared and an amplitude dependent on the temporal period.
the front speeds in reaction-diffusion equations are enhanced by the shear flow and that the enhancement is proportional to the square and the linear amplitude of the mean zero shear.

the front speed in reaction diffusion equations in the presence of space-time mean zero periodic shear flow is enhanced by an amount that depends on the shear amplitude squared at small amplitude, and by an amount that is proportional to the shear amplitude itself at large amplitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of shear flows on the propagation speeds of traveling fronts for two dimensional reaction-diffusive systems.
the effects of spatial-temporal shear on reaction-diffusion fronts in two-dimensional space.
the study of reaction-diffusion equations in spatially and/or temporally periodic flows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

shear enhances the front speeds, the extent of enhancement is a monotonic decreasing function of the shear temporal frequency, the extent is a decreasing function of the reaction nonlinearity strength, and the enhancement is proportional to the square of shear amplitude at small amplitudes and proportional to shear amplitude at large amplitudes.

, at small shear amplitudess, front speeds increase proportional to shear amplitude square and are decreasing with increasing shear frequencies, and at large shear amplitudesses, front speeds increase with shear amplitude linearly and are again decreasing in shear frequency.
the front speeds are enhanced through mean zero spatially periodic shearing flows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the front speed enhancement by the shear is a non-monotonic function of the shear strength and the shear temporal frequency.
the front speeds through space-time periodic shear flows are always larger than those through space periodic shear flows.

the reaction-diffusion fronts speed through spatially-periodic shear flows is a linear function of shear amplitude squared at small shear amplitude and is a linear function in shear amplitude at large shear amplitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shear flows can significantly enhance the front speeds in reaction-diffusion systems, even when the shear is weak.
the effect of the shear is more pronounced for larger temporal frequencies, which is in agreement with previous results.
the front speed enhancements due to spatial and/or space-time shears can be predicted using simple and explicit formulas.
